- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model over-forecasts; reduce forecast by 1–2% of recent mean.
- Model consistently over-estimates prices after sharp upward spikes (e.g., >70.00) — cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- Model under-estimates prices during prolonged downward sentiment — add 1–3% buffer to forecast if sentiment remains negative for 3+ consecutive days.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: model often misses 1–3 day trend shifts — apply 1-day lag correction by aligning with 28d or 30d true outcome.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence; if below, add 1–2% per day.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +0.67 to -0.33) triggers immediate downward adjustment — reduce forecast by 2–5% of recent mean for next 3 days.
